To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) mobile 2FA is vulnerable to a variety of attacks that allow an attacker to impersonate a victim, and (ii) the attacks can be prevented by a variety of countermeasures that are either already deployed in practice or are straightforward to deploy.

(1) mobile 2FA systems can be attacked, (2) the security of mobile 2FA is highly sensitive to the choice of secondary authentication token, (3) the security of the most popular 2FA systems is questionable and can be improved, (4) the security of a few 2FA systems has been improved by their developers, and (5) some 2FA systems are secure by design.

(i) the security of the mobile two-factor authentication schemes can be improved by adding the user's device to the list of authentication factors, and (ii) the mobile two-factor schemes can be further improved by using a more complex authentication token, such as a password or PIN.
